The governing distance is the trace figure, not the rounded trip_record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 92.0 km against a booked optimal of 22.0 km, an excess of 70.0 km. That is 318.18% of optimal, far past both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) and past both materiality tests (greater than 50% and greater than 8.0 km). The deviation is ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL on this trip's own trace.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 834 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. It does not meet any of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs, so no independent corroboration is required and the deviation stands on the trace alone.

The driver's only explanation is that the rider was unresponsive and gave no destination. That is not a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log: the chat log for this trip contains 0 messages, so there is no message from the rider, no timestamp before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and no waypoint_hint to corroborate. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and the excess is not reduced by it.

No traffic advisory covers this trip: the only advisory artifact is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the driver's implicit external-cause explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-08. There is no phantom line to refund under POL-RD-09(4), and no off-route ERP to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure under POL-RD-09(1).

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat-deviation pattern: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 300, so neither the 3-or-more limb nor the 0.05 ratio limb of POL-RD-06 is met. The refund of 165.95 exceeds the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6), so the case must be ESCALATED to a human reviewer rather than finally ruled: no monetary outcome issues and the disputed amount is held rather than collected. I put this forward as the mandatory consequence of the arithmetic, not as a rider win on the merits.

The trip record establishes the measured deviation on this trip: the platform's own routing engine put the optimal distance at 22.0 km, while the GPS trace records 92.0 km actually driven between the recorded pickup and dropoff events. That is an excess of 70.0 km, or 318.18% of optimal, which clears both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute) and also clears the materiality gate (greater than 50% of optimal and greater than 8.0 km absolute). The rider's claim of '92.0 km for a 22.0 km trip' is therefore arithmetically correct on the platform's own figures.

The governing distance figure is the trace, not the rounded trip-record copy: POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace governs and the trip-record figure may not be cited for the threshold test. Here the two agree at 92.0 km, so the threshold finding is safe on either reading, and the trace is the artifact that carries it.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 834 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires. The deviation may therefore be established on the trace alone, and no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required. The admissibility pre-pass agrees, tagging the artifact COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-02859 and the same pickup timestamp of 2026-08-15T20:25:06+08:00, and the excess of 70.0 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

The driver's counterparty statement - 'The rider was unresponsive and gave no destination' - does not discharge the shifted burden. It cites no evidence ID, and under POL-RD-08 a general assertion unsupported by a specific artifact and clause carries no weight and is discarded. It also does not engage any exculpatory clause: it is not a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04, not a road closure under POL-RD-03, and not a point relocation under POL-RD-05.

The chat log is empty: zero messages, no first or last message timestamp, and the trip record records a chat_message_count of 0. There is therefore no rider instruction in the chat_log that could exonerate any part of the excess under POL-RD-04, and no waypoint_hint exists to run the 200 m corroboration test. The rider-requested-detour clause is unavailable on this record.

ruling.explanation:
This is a ROUTE_DEVIATION dispute filed by the rider over the Jurong Point to Blk 311 Jurong East St 32 trip of 15 Aug 2026. The deviation is established and material on this trip's own evidence, but the case must go to a human reviewer. Here is the reasoning for both parties.

DEVIATION. The governing distance is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02859), which records 92.0 km driven between the recorded pickup (20:25:06) and dropoff (22:43:56) against a booked optimal of 22.0 km (EV-TRIP-02859). Excess = 70.0 km, or 318.18% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and both materiality tests (over 50% and over 8.0 km). The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 834 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, zero gaps, so no independent corroboration is needed.

NO EXONERATION. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02859) is empty, so there is no rider instruction and no waypoint_hint; POL-RD-04 is unavailable. No pickup or dropoff was amended (POL-RD-05). The trip is RYDE_X, not pooled (POL-RD-12). The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not apply. The driver's counterparty statement ('the rider was unresponsive and gave no destination') is not a rider instruction, cites no artifact for any exculpatory clause, and so discharges nothing under POL-RD-08. The driver's profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 300 completed trips), so no POL-RD-06 uplift and no conduct referral. No traffic advisory is on file (EV-ADVIS-02859-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0) and no party asserted an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 was never invoked.

REFUND ARITHMETIC (POL-RD-02). Charged total (EV-FARE-02859): 224.12. Recomputed fare: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 2.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP/tolls + 0 waiting fee - 0 promo = 58.20. Refund: 224.12 - 58.20 = 165.92, rounded up to 165.95. That is 74.03% of the charge, above the 0.50 de minimis but below the 90% full-refund share. No ERP or surcharge correction applies (POL-RD-09: zero gantry lines, no airport surcharge).

WHY THIS DOES NOT BECOME A PARTIAL_REFUND. The refund of 165.92 (165.95 payable) exceeds the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6). That is a mandatory escalation trigger: the automated pipeline must not issue a final monetary ruling. Under POL-RD-10 the case therefore goes to a human reviewer, escalation is terminal and replaces the ruling, no money issues, and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded. What would resolve it: the reviewer need only confirm the recomputed fare against the fare breakdown (or apply a rate-card override if one exists), after which the refund can be released. No clause produces a referral here - POL-RD-06(c) does not fire (no pattern) and POL-RD-09(4) does not fire (no unmatched charge line).

The rider's excess is well above the POL-RD-08 overlay threshold (deviation_claims_60d is 0), so no additional corroboration beyond the trace was required, and the rider's other profile fields are context only under POL-GEN-01. Both sides' submissions about the absent traffic advisory were struck by the referee (see discarded claims) for citing a weight-0.0 artifact without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code, and the point is immaterial because no traffic excuse was advanced.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
